item.description:
4.2.26 2:25 am
Q: bro i had a disappointing ass dinner. the server kept hyping us up abt how the food uses so many spices therefore it's super flavorful. Tell me WHERE were the spices when i got my entree because that shit was BLAND AS FUCK & the whole appeal of the restaurant was that it's supposed to be flavorful moroccan cuisine. is the flavor in the room with us because it must still be in morocco. have you had a similar experience recently?? What would you do in this situation??
A: there is something particularly humorous about something being hyped way up and then actually being the opposite of what it's hyped to be. this reminds me many many years ago at burger thing, when they first introduced the "chicken fries" (or maybe one of the many times the re-introduced them), they come in a tall, top-heavy box. the box is somehow designed so it has a sauce holder on top. a little slot where you can put the sauce container. They had arrows pointing to it and then had a description "Sauce goes here. Yup, we promoted the guy who invented it." whether or not they actually promoted someone, i dont know or care, but here's the thing: the sauce fits fine in the slot, but as soon as you start taking the fries out, to eat them, the box immediately falls over. it only works when the box is full of chicken fries. this brilliant invention immediately fails as soon as you start using it. What would have seemed mildly silly, became an even more humorous spectacle based on the hype story written on the box. i'm also thinking of debut of the tesla cybertruck, where they demonstrated the unbreakable windows by hitting it with a sledge hammer and the window immediately broke "what you do in this situation" is you collect stories like this for amusement

item.title: What's going on in the everybody wants to rule the world drum part?
item.description:

Q: What's going on in the everybody wants to rule the world drum part?
A: you have a triplet feel (you can say it's 4/4 with triplets, or you can say it's 12/8 with eight notes, or even 6/8 depending on how big you want the bars to be on paper), you have 4-on-the-floor, which means the kick drum is hitting all 4 beats, you have snare on 2 and 4 ('backbeat'), and then perhaps what you want to know most is the percussion, there is a percussion accent happening on alternating triplets. which makes a cool pattern when you accent one out of every 2 notes when the notes are grouped in groups of 3. so if you're counting "1 trip let 2 trip let 3 trip let 4 trip let", the percussion accents (the louder notes in the tambourine or shaker or whatever) will occur on "one TRIP let TWO trip LET three TRIP let FOUR trip LET". at least this is what i recall happening. i havent really listened to the song since i saw it in the credits for marty surpreme in the cinema, but the song has been around for decades and i've heard it plenty, and to my best recollection that is what the drums and perc are doing. and the snare will give you some nice fills at the end of the 8 or 16 bar segments, usually "BAP BAP _ BAP BAP BAP" in the last two beats (or the last 6 subdivisions). hopefully my language is more or less intelligible to you. i'm trying to be broad in terms of catering the different kinds of musical or mathematical literacy you may be working with

item.title: what is the story of when you made "La de da de da de da de day oh"?
item.description:
4.17.26 11:00 pm
Q: what is the story of when you made "La de da de da de da de day oh"?
A: ok so in 2009 i finally got fed up with the fact that i didnt seem to be writing any songs despite the fact that i felt like i had more than enough skills to be able to do so. so as a last resort i deeply downgraded my standards and just started scribbling garbage on paper. i wrote a beginning about 'i dont have enough time to say the things i want to say' etc, something very much resembling the first verse you'd recognize from that song. (but also not quite the same). that song lived only on paper and also didnt have the 'la de da' chorus, it did something else instead and ended after about a minute and a half. fast foward to 2012 i finally got fed up with how much songwriting i had done without knowing how to organize it or choose which ones to work on. so i built a master list of everything i had, in order of when it was written, and then i started working on each one. the "i dont have enough time" bit came up, and i fixed the verse, and wrote a chorus (the "la de da" chorus that you would recognize). fast forward to 2017, i'd figured out how to finish and produce songs, but i was really fed up with how long it took. i was trying out a 2-week schedule, alternating between song and not-song, always with a video, alternating whether or not i appear on camera in the video. it SEEMED to work ok with a non-song video called 'soap tips', and next would be to do a song video with me appearing in it. i should have known that this would be impossible in 2 weeks but i tried it anyway. on the selection process i landed on the 'la de da' song, which still hadnt been updated since 2012, so it had just 1 verse and chorus written. BUT.... the day after selection, i started doubting the selection. i actually wanted to switch to a different song. then i went to get a haircut and i was thinking about the selection, as thinking about the 'la de da' song again, and then for some reason just at the moment i was getting into the chair, (songwriting loves to work like this) the first 3 lines of the second verse just rammed itself into my head. so with that momentum i figured ok that's the selection, then at home i finished writing the rest. then i recorded it, made the video, etc, and it all took way way way way way way longer than 2 weeks

item.title: i guess im a big fat liar because i like to say i just make art for myself and other people's opinions are whatever but really im horrified by ai because it can convincingly duplicate all the things i pour real emotion into and the only defense i can offer for my own work is "well i actually did put emotion into it" which is true but no one really cares about because the end result is the same to them. any tips on being less of a big fat liar?

A: well, this issue can of course be maximum confusing for everyone, at least for now while we get used to it and learn to understand what it is, what it's not, and what it means and doesnt mean. However, it's not nearly as bad as you think, and in some ways it's absolutely wonderful. let me just disect one of your points here: you say no one cares because the end result is the same..... Even if that's true, imagine if the quantity was cranked up to a trillion. whatever becomes overflowingly abundant becomes de-valued. so now no one cares about the fake version either, just because there is SO much of it, it becomes worthless. now, true, also, that that also means that it devalues any kind of thing that SOUNDS LIKE something the machines would cough up, and that may be considered unfortunate for human people who were making.... lets say 'normalish' music before, .... but the effect that this has on everyone is it cultivates a huge thirst for something new and different. whatever it is that the machines cant cough up, that's what will be desired. this has always been true, but now it's accelerated. yes, people will be using the machines in all kinds of ways up down and sideways, in fantastically creative ways (which perhaps older people will not quite understand), and then at the same time there will also be some people that just choose not to use it, and they reap some pretty crazy advantages from NOT using it. in many ways this is analogous to the invention of synths, the invention of drum machines, the invention of SAMPLING ("effortless, he just stole someone elses song and rapped over it!"), PITCH-CORRECTED VOCALS ("but she cant even sing, shes not a real singer" etc), and so on. All these may be horrifying concepts at first, but the advantages are very genuine, AND the benefits of NOT using them are also genuine. AND, also true, the major thing that really truly moves the needle is CONNECTION with audiences. so as long as your audience is human, they are going to care deeply about the human presence in the art. Difficult to prove at times, yes, this may be. but that is also a very fun and interesting game that will become EXTREMELY satisfying to win, for both the artist and the audience. that being said, i will not be using it at all, for the forseeable future. similar to my decision not to use loops, and not to use any pitch correction. this is certainly not to frown on anyone who does, it's just that i have some very interesting skills in terms of songwriting and playing, which can be used very much to my advantage. The key, of course, is to steer it clear of the generic. For weirdo artists like me, for example, it's a license to not be ashamed of being weird and different. If there ever was any pressure to "try to sound commercial" or "try to sound like what's popular", this new technology will SHATTER that bland obligation, better than i think anything else ever could. being a sentient ass human being is a priceless commodity in art, and its value is now thrust to center stage more than it ever has been before, as any and all mechanical aspects are trivialized and removed from the equation. as usual it reminds me of almost every major invention of yester year
